review: The Arabic uses parentheses to mark a leader/congregation split (عَلِّمْنِي ... / فَلَيْسَ لِي). The reader prints bare lines, so the parentheses are dropped and the speaker shift is kept only by the syntax — each stanza still turns from petition to confession at line 3.
1:2 הוֹדִיעֵנִי נָא דַּרְכֶּךָ — Exodus 33:13, kept as a quotation; the Arabic has رُؤْيَتَكَ لِلدَّرْب ('Your sight for the way'), which Hebrew renders as knowing the way rather than seeing it.
1:3 מִשְׁעָן — 'support', biblical (Isa 3:1 מִשְׁעָן וּמַשְׁעֵנָה), for سَنَد.
1:5 דְבָרְךָ נֵר לְרַגְלִי — Psalm 119:105, verbatim except for the word order needed by the tune (the psalm has נֵר־לְרַגְלִי דְבָרֶךָ).
2:3 חֶבֶל הַיְשׁוּעָה — 'the cord of salvation'; חֶבֶל is the biblical cord (Ps 16:6), and the Arabic طَوْق (collar/band) has no closer Hebrew equivalent.
